title: Open WebUI skill mention parsing -- T1499 unclosed <$ triggers quadratic backtracking, blocks event loop
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-59220 (GHSA-ffpj-xv5c-p3gw,
CVSS 6.5 MEDIUM), affecting Open WebUI from 0.9.2 before 0.10.0.

`SKILL_MENTION_RE` and `strip_re` in
`backend/open_webui/utils/middleware.py` parse `<$skillId|label>`
skill-mention syntax in chat messages using OVERLAPPING QUANTIFIERS.
An authenticated chat message containing `<$` with NO closing `>`
triggers quadratic (or worse) backtracking in these regexes -- and
because Open WebUI processes this parsing on the shared `asyncio`
event loop, one such message BLOCKS the loop for every other request
the server is handling, not just the sender's own.

Detection logic flags a chat message body containing the literal
sequence `<$` with no corresponding closing `>` within a reasonable
span -- the exact malformed-but-plausible-looking syntax this
advisory's regex bug reacts catastrophically to.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (open-webui, via
GHSA and NVD, citing the exact regex names and source file), fixed in
0.10.0.
